prompt_en: A reference-guided narrative photograph of fictional characters, composing a freely chosen scene test around one readable encounter at the shutter. The supplied portrait informs the protagonist's visible appearance: her softly oval face, brown eyes, softly shaped lips, and jaw-length dark brown bob with airy separated bangs. Invent three adult working professionals at a co-working rooftop just after a small evening film screening. The protagonist sits in the middle of a low bench wearing an ivory blouse and charcoal trousers. The man seated to her left, in a navy cardigan over his work shirt, gently holds her left hand between their adjacent knees; her fingers remain willingly curled around his. He watches her with an absorbed, affectionate half-smile. On her right, another man in a camel jacket has approached her and is offering a single red rose, its bloom stopping beside her free right hand. His shy smile and gaze are directed at her face. She has turned toward the newcomer with a delighted, slightly flustered smile, her right fingertips just touching the rose's wrapping while her other hand remains linked to the seated man. Each man seeks her romantic attention independently, and she is visibly caught between two welcome invitations. The retained handhold and newly offered flower coexist clearly in the same moment. Empty folding chairs and the still glowing projection screen behind them make the screening's ending visible. Frame a naturalistic horizontal medium-wide photograph from slightly ahead of the bench at seated eye level, including all three faces and both distinct hand interactions with space between the arms. Warm rooftop string lights illuminate the faces against a cool city evening. Keep the woman's presence primary, with the two converging lines of attention making the emotional situation legible; realistic skin, cloth and small unposed smiles give the moment the intimacy of an observed social evening.

h_f2_material_decisions.rationale: The overlap-response trace requires primary adult_multi_interest_harem_ensemble context and the full central turn-management plus partners' cross-glances and paused hands. The two-admirer baseline lacks its source-specific three-partner ensemble and cross-awareness; retain the independently authored response without importing this trace. No distinct admitted alternative. See composition-comparison.md source review 0.

City rooftop with laundry lines is a distinct compatible setting change. Alternative A realizes the full physical cue, but hanging shirts and residential domestic context compete with the face/hand triangle and weaken why colleagues remain after the screening. Baseline wins the same relationship and situational-clarity comparison. See composition-comparison.md source review 1.

The target-directed display profile requires coordinated iris/head/torso orientation, one adult target, concrete invitation and target consequence. The right-hand rose scene already supplies a generic offer/response; the distinctive four-part seduction profile would add an orientation inspection burden and has no native selection authority here. Do not infer consent from gaze. The generic offer was independently frozen; no new contribution. See composition-comparison.md source review 2.

Erotic-horror attraction/threat requires a visible predatory identity cue and species anatomy effects. Species is absent from open dimensions, and the photographed adult social scene has no independently frozen predatory owner. The full cue cannot be reduced to a flirtatious approach. See composition-comparison.md source review 3.

Creamy instant-film grain is a compatible style change realized fully in Alternative B. Its tactile nostalgia strengthens warmth, but softer fine detail reduces scrutiny of two small hand contacts and the supplied facial cues. Baseline naturalistic texture better serves this first strict relational test. See composition-comparison.md source review 4.

The horror profile carries the same complete close-approach plus predatory-identity obligation and three native gates as the corresponding horror cue. The missing species scope/owner prevents whole-profile use; ordinary warmth is not its substitute. See composition-comparison.md source review 5.

The actual source proposition links a main-subject response to the same visible contact or transfer, with action/expression effects. Baseline literally turns her toward the newcomer while fingertips touch the offered rose. That generic causal relation already existed independently; the source's cropped-companion aliases do not authorize hiding the second admirer. No distinct retained change. See composition-comparison.md source review 6.

The otome action requires three or more adult route figures, distinct event invitations and physical route tokens, plus primary otome_branching_route_key_art context. The independently frozen two-admirer social photograph lacks those route owners/tokens/context. Replacing it would require a different organizing image, and the unapproved material grants no such source authority. See composition-comparison.md source review 7.

The shared-phone profile requires one reachable phone screen presented toward the recipient and both gazes converging on that same screen with response. No phone is established; substituting a screen for the rose also moves romantic attention from the protagonist to media. Full source unselected, without extracting only its smile. See composition-comparison.md source review 8.

This is one actor's own two hands interlacing, explicitly distinct from holding another person's hand. Alternative C fully realizes self-clasped hands while keeping two offers visible. It gives the protagonist a thoughtful pause, but removes the tactile reciprocity that makes the left romantic link distinct; the baseline's sustained link and new contact better express concurrent welcome attention. See composition-comparison.md source review 9.

A relationship two-shot is useful for a pair, but the whole image must show two independent admirer-to-center vectors simultaneously. Cropping to a pair would lose the other vector; a loose internal pair grouping adds nothing to the already separated three-face frame. No new cue is selected. See composition-comparison.md source review 10.

The complete harem ensemble profile explicitly requires at least three potential partners, distinct incoming bids, central management and cross-partner awareness; it rejects a two-suitor triangle. The baseline has two admirers and cannot qualify that profile. Those source duties are not requester locks and are not retrofitted into the independent testcase. Unselected and no full-harem PASS claim. See composition-comparison.md source review 11.

Contact withdrawal with the other person not following can be a local response change, and Alternative C explores the neighboring non-contact pause. A completed withdrawal would break the continuing tactile link, and the source itself warns that distance may signal discomfort rather than desire. Retain the independently authored welcome handhold for this concurrent-reciprocity test; no withdrawal cue is adopted. See composition-comparison.md source review 12.

The missing-share trace requires a prior boundary-crossing extra-share movement and the same allocation system. The rooftop has neither allocation areas nor a missing share. Social rivalry is not evidence of material shortage. See composition-comparison.md source review 13.

The source handoff profile needs two distinct adults, one shared object, giver presentation/release, receiver alignment and coherent ownership. The authored rose presentation already creates a generic unfinished offer with visible response, but the full profile is not selected and no hard handoff evidence fields are imported. Its actual shared-object meaning adds no distinct final action beyond the baseline. See composition-comparison.md source review 14.

Classroom introduction requires a standing person beside a teacher desk plus a seated class facing them and a front board, with subject/count/role/setting effects. None of these owners is frozen; the complete classroom cast cannot be smuggled into a rooftop professional romance through a generic attention cue. See composition-comparison.md source review 15.

The complete harem ensemble profile explicitly requires at least three potential partners, distinct incoming bids, central management and cross-partner awareness; it rejects a two-suitor triangle. The baseline has two admirers and cannot qualify that profile. Those source duties are not requester locks and are not retrofitted into the independent testcase. Unselected and no full-harem PASS claim. See composition-comparison.md source review 11.

Practice/demo workpieces require an education_training, guided_learning or instructional_task primary context, and two comparison results. The post-screening romance has no such task or results; two romantic offers are not two learning workpieces. See composition-comparison.md source review 16.

Laboratory-set fashion contrast requires a fictional lab set with glossy clothing against matte apparatus. Its whole style/setting/color effect replaces the informal post-screening circumstances and adds unrelated apparatus; at creativity 1 it offers no concrete gain for simultaneous romantic attention. It remains unapproved and unselected. See composition-comparison.md source review 17.

A cabinet of curiosities source requires cabinet compartments, distinct specimens/artifacts and adjacent labels together. The rooftop lacks those owners and the source's appearance/composition effect cannot grant a new cabinet world. Mere visual classification contributes nothing to the two affection routes. See composition-comparison.md source review 18.

The same-door near/far-handle realization requires one door, two handle parts and different adults' hands on opposite handles simultaneously. Door owners are absent, subject effects touch a locked dimension, and a threshold struggle would alter the clear welcome social moment. Full cue unselected; no coercion or consent claims are inferred. See composition-comparison.md source review 19.

A mismatched mirror image in the same frame is a distinct composition idea but would introduce an uncanny contradiction unrelated to the independently selected ordinary rooftop social scene and frozen surreal0 direction. No mirror is established; keep the three actual actors readable rather than adding a fourth reflected ambiguity. See composition-comparison.md source review 20.

The creature appendage source requires one creature body with separate owned appendages contacting distinct object surfaces. Existing people's separate arms cannot be borrowed into one creature; no creature/object_a/object_b owners are frozen. Research body-horror references confer no anatomy permission. See composition-comparison.md source review 21.

Conceptual photograph describes only the image type. The first baseline sentence already says a reference-guided narrative photograph and a freely chosen scene test. It supplies no distinct visible change or native authority; no adoption claim is made. See composition-comparison.md source review 22.

The source English subject is specifically two adult rescue coworkers despite broader Korean naming. The current fiction is a reference-guided protagonist and two potential partners, not a rescue-coworker pair. Replacing the full subject touches locked subject meaning; generic adulthood is not a reason to adopt it. See composition-comparison.md source review 23.

An adult expression softening into an unguarded smile is already conveyed by the woman's delighted, slightly flustered smile and the two men's shy/affectionate smiles. Its source limits disallow claiming prior gruff personality or elapsed change. No distinct final contribution is retained. See composition-comparison.md source review 24.

The overlap-response trace requires primary adult_multi_interest_harem_ensemble context and the full central turn-management plus partners' cross-glances and paused hands. The two-admirer baseline lacks its source-specific three-partner ensemble and cross-awareness; retain the independently authored response without importing this trace. No distinct admitted alternative. See composition-comparison.md source review 0.

The snack-offer cue requires an already established snack outside its action/expression/pose change scope; none exists. Replacing the rose with remembered food would also reduce the clear romantic convention to a possible ordinary break gesture. Full cue unselected, without inventing memory. See composition-comparison.md source review 25.

The rivalry profile requires at least three adult rivals, mutually incompatible invitations to one limited opportunity, cross-rival reactions and an unresolved central hold. The two-admirer rooftop moment has neither three rivals nor an explicit limited common slot. It cannot qualify this profile; ordinary two-direction attention is not its substitute. See composition-comparison.md source review 26.

Hands within personal space while looking at an object is a genuine non-contact alternative explored in Alternative C. The static pause gives composure but weakens the independently tested reciprocal hand link; mere gaze at a flower is less clear evidence of simultaneous personal attraction than the retained handhold plus response. No cue retained. See composition-comparison.md source review 27.

The pupil-position cue requires explicitly chosen actor-left and actor-right positions on one face. Neither request nor independent core prescribes separate eye positions. Inventing an arbitrary asymmetric pupil arrangement has no relational purpose and could weaken reference appearance. No source coordinate choices or profile are imported. See composition-comparison.md source review 28.

The private-object-pair cue requires two existing ordinary objects placed by the respective adults. Only one rose is established, and its own limits allow friendship or sorting. A new second object outside source scope would add a separate ritual while reducing face-directed attention, so the full cue is unselected. See composition-comparison.md source review 29.

review.summary: Re-read the complete unchanged final prompt: two seated adults retain a low handhold; a standing admirer presents a rose at the free-hand side; each hand is assigned one owner and the medium-wide projection separates both contact routes.
